newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia sees progress in N.Africa free trade zone.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia sees progress in N.Africa free trade zone.

text.p: Tunisia has signed a free trade zone accord with Morocco, proposed to Algeria one similar accord to Algeria, and has a de facto free trade zone with Libya, Tunisian Industry Minister Slaheddine Bouguerra said on Thursday.
"We are also revising our bilateral accords with Mediterranean countries to have them adapt to a free trade zone with them," Bouguerra also told a Mediterranean investment meeting in Tunis.

"We have signed a free trade zone accord with Morocco. We have told Algeria that we are ready to sign one immediately and to dismantle customs barriers. We have with Libya a de facto free trade zone," he said.
The trade accord with Morocco was signed at the end of last year.

Tunisia, Morocco, Algeria, Libya and Mauritania are members of the Arab Maghreb Union set up in 1989 with the aim of forming an economic grouping. Among its aims was a free trade zone for the five North African countries.
Officials said that Tunisia was discussing with Egypt and Jordan free trade zone accords.
Tunisia in 1995 signed its first free trade zone accord with the European Union.
